move: phones drop one by one into a 3D staircase, scroll, fall away
how: Over a drifting aurora background, six 230x500 phones (alternating light/dark UI) drop from 700px above their staircase position (x 110+112i, y -100+40i, z -90i, all rotateY -26) with rotateX 20 and opacity 0, settling with back.out(1.2) over 1.1s, staggered 0.22s starting at 2% of the 10s. A three-word headline rises from yPercent 110 (0.1s stagger, expo.out) at 5% with a paragraph after. From 15% the whole staircase slides x -60 and turns rotateY 8 over 5.5s sine.inOut while each screen body scrolls y -110 and back (power3.inOut, 0.16s wave) between 30% and 70%. At 84% phones fall y +=700 with rotateX -20 and fade (expo.in, 0.14s stagger) and the copy slides off left.
adapt: Change N, the screen names, hero gradients and copy, the headline words and the background image; the step() function sets the stair spacing. Keep the 1.1s back.out(1.2) drops with 0.22s stagger and the 5.5s sine sway.
port: mount(el, shot) builds .cas with N phones from shot.screens; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with drops at (0.02 + i*0.022)*D, sway at 0.15D, scrolls at 0.3D/0.56D and the fall at 0.84D. The copy from() tweens should become fromTo with immediateRender:false; el needs perspective:1800px and .cas preserve-3d.
caveats: catalog lists 12s but the file renders 10s
full-frame background image with brightness/saturate filter
